title: tSDK: shape-inference and 'Zodizer' helpers for discriminated output + streaming ergonomics
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Consumers of the TypeScript SDK (tSDK) need a low-friction way to declare structured output contracts that work for both non-streaming and streaming responses. Current patterns require repetitive Zod schemas and manual runtime guards when discriminated unions and streaming chunks are involved. This ticket proposes a small set of developer-facing utilities ("Zodizer" + shape-inference helpers) that: 1) infer lightweight discriminators from JSON-Schema/Zod shapes, 2) produce runtime validators usable for streaming chunk validation, and 3) generate TypeScript type aliases for dev ergonomics (no duplicate type declarations). Goals: reduce boilerplate for typical structured-output use cases; make streaming validation robust (per-chunk validation + permissive merge strategy); provide clear migration path for existing tsdk consumers. Non-goals: full schema registry service or first-class contract negotiation protocols.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A small public utilities API exported from @redwood/tsdk: zodize(schema), inferDiscriminator(schema), streamingValidator(schema, options). 2) zodize(schema) returns (a) a Zod schema for runtime validation and (b) a TypeScript type exported via helper types so consumers get compile-time types without hand-writing interfaces. 3) streamingValidator can accept partial-chunk objects, validate known fields, and produce a deterministic merge result or clear validation error. 4) Automated unit tests covering discriminated unions with 3 variants, nested objects and array-of-objects, and token-delimited streaming. 5) Example consumer doc + runnable example in examples/structured-output/ that demonstrates non-streaming and streaming usage. 6) Backwards-compatible: consumers using previous pattern should continue to work (adapter helpers provided).

notes: Design decisions: prefer Zod-first approach because runtime validation is mandatory for streaming and Zod has best ergonomics for the team. We'll provide a thin JSON-Schema adapter for teams that require JSON-Schema artifacts. Streaming behavior: validator will accept partial objects (missing fields) and will expose a 'finalize' method to do strict validation once model completes. Security: no secrets in schemas; runtime validation does not influence request routing directly (only local post-processing).
implementation_plan: 1) Build zodize util that accepts either a Zod schema or a lightweight JSON-like declarative shape and returns a canonical Zod schema + TS helper types. 2) Implement inferDiscriminator: walk schema to find candidate fields ("type","kind","_tag", or user-configured) or synthesize a discriminator. 3) Implement streamingValidator with incremental state and mergeStrategy options. 4) Add unit + integration tests and examples; add docs and migration notes. 5) Release as part of tsdk-2025.07 with migration guide.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: models sometimes emit malformed partial chunks that break strict validators. Mitigation: default permissive streamingValidator mode, clear docs, and opt-in strict finalization. Risk: adding API surface increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep helpers minimal (3 top-level exports) and provide adapters for existing internal patterns.
test_plan: Unit tests for zodize with: discriminated unions, optional nested fields, arrays, and JSON-schema adapter. Streaming tests: simulate token-delimited partials, corrupted fields, and finalize behavior. E2E: example app in examples/structured-output/ exercises a canary model that emits a discriminated union across streaming tokens. CI: require Node 18 target matrix and maintain a baseline for Zod versions.
out_of_scope: Python/Go SDK bindings (will be follow-ups), schema registry integration, or server-side enforcement of contracts.
